parsed_response.reasoning: Verifiable from the diff: packages/types/Calendar.d.ts changes the Calendar interface to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)`, and GoogleCalendarService is the only implementation updated to accept credentialId (`async createEvent(calEventRaw: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)`). LarkCalendarService still declares `async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` and Office365/BaseCalendarService likewise keep the one-parameter signature, so the per-credential destination-calendar lookup (`cal.credentialId === credentialId`) exists only in Google. This is a real, specific incomplete-migration/interface-drift concern grounded in the diff (TS method bivariance masks it), not a hallucination. It is not clearly a runtime bug since the EventManager loop still invokes createEvent per credential and non-Google providers fall back to the first destination calendar, so the concrete defect claim ('silent no-op') is overstated — but the contract drift itself is substantive and review-relevant.

judged_text: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId) but only the Google implementation was updated; every other Calendar implementation in the repo (BaseCalendarService subclasses, other app-store calendars) still implements the one-parameter signature and ignores credentialId. Any future caller relying on the interface contract to select a per-credential destination calendar gets silent no-op behavior from every non-Google provider; TypeScript method bivariance hides this today, so nothing flags the drift at compile time. The next person touching createEvent gets harder-to-trace behavior across providers.
